The CPU is the brain of the computer. It is the part of the computer that executes instructions. The CPU is made up of a control unit and an arithmetic logic unit. The control unit is responsible for fetching instructions from memory and decoding them. The arithmetic logic unit is responsible for executing the instructions.

The CPU executes instructions in a step-by-step process. First, the control unit fetches an instruction from memory. The instruction is then decoded by the control unit. The arithmetic logic unit then executes the instruction. Finally, the results of the instruction are stored in memory.
